<reason>B built the stronger distinction between chosen fictional attachment and seller-directed exploitation of personal vulnerabilities. It directly answered objections about output review and regulatory scope, acknowledging limited constraints around subscription decisions rather than promising costless regulation. A raised a legitimate chilling-effects concern, but largely asserted that restricting targeted payment pressure would destroy the requested companionship. B more convincingly explained why honest prices and a working exit do not exhaust providers’ responsibilities.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s pressure question elicited A’s explicit permission for exploiting disclosed abandonment fears when cancellation works. B then distinguished consent to fictional jealousy from authorization for personalized sales pressure, exposing the central weakness in A’s proposed safeguards.</best_rebuttal>
